objects.description: Clipboard format identifier type. An alias of size_t used to identify registered clipboard formats.

RAII clipboard lock for low-level access. Constructing tries to open/lock the system clipboard (optionally using a native window handle), and destruction unlocks it. Provides methods to clear, query/transfer arbitrary formats and images. Implementation is pimpl-hidden in lock::impl.
Error codes reported by the library via error handlers. CannotLock indicates failure to lock the clipboard; ImageNotSupported indicates lack of image support for the current platform/format.
Function pointer type for receiving asynchronous/synchronous error notifications from the library. The callback takes a single ErrorCode.

Describes image layout and pixel format used by clip::image: dimensions, row stride, and bit masks/shifts for RGBA channels. required_data_size() returns the buffer size needed for the current spec. Used to interpret raw pixel data in straight (non-premultiplied) alpha.

Owns or wraps raw pixel data described by an image_spec. Guarantees straight (non-premultiplied) alpha externally; platform-specific conversions may occur internally. Supports default, spec-based, data+spec, copy, and move construction; provides access to raw data and spec, validity checks, and reset. Manages ownership via m_own_data.

functions.name: clip::lock::lock
functions.description: Constructs a clipboard lock that attempts to open/lock the system clipboard for exclusive access. On Windows, you may pass your current HWND as native_window_handle to help OpenClipboard/SetClipboardData succeed after EmptyClipboard; passing nullptr is also supported. Use locked() to check whether the lock was acquired before calling other member functions to modify/read clipboard content.
requirements: Should be constructed before calling other low-level clipboard methods on this lock instance.
On Windows, passing a valid HWND as native_window_handle may be required to avoid SetClipboardData failing after EmptyClipboard (per header comment); nullptr is allowed.
Call locked() and ensure it returns true before using methods like clear/set_data/get_data/set_image/get_image on this instance.

functions.name: clip::lock::~lock
functions.description: Destructor that unlocks/releases the clipboard if it was successfully locked in the constructor. Ensures cleanup of clipboard access state.
requirements: Do not use the lock instance after it has been destroyed.
Other clipboard operations that require a lock must occur before destruction.

functions.name: clip::lock::locked
functions.description: Returns true if the clipboard was successfully locked by this object’s constructor. Use to guard subsequent clipboard operations on this lock instance.
requirements: Must be called on a valid clip::lock instance.
If this returns false, callers should not invoke clear/set_data/get_data/set_image/get_image on this lock.

functions.name: clip::lock::clear
functions.description: Clears the current clipboard content for the active clipboard/pasteboard. Prevents previous unknown formats from persisting after unlock.
requirements: A successful lock must be held (locked() must be true) on this object.

functions.name: clip::lock::is_convertible
functions.description: Returns true if the current clipboard contents can be converted to the specified format identifier.
requirements: A successful lock should be held (locked() == true) to query the clipboard state.
The format identifier must be one obtained from register_format() or a known built-in format such as text_format() or image_format().

functions.name: clip::lock::set_data
functions.signature: bool clip::lock::set_data(clip::format f, const char* buf, size_t len)
functions.description: Sets raw clipboard data in the specified format for the currently locked clipboard. Use with custom registered formats or known formats.
requirements: A successful lock must be held (locked() must be true).
f must be a valid format identifier (e.g., from register_format(), text_format(), image_format()).
buf must point to at least len bytes of readable memory.
len must equal the size of the data being provided.

functions.name: clip::lock::get_data
functions.signature: bool clip::lock::get_data(clip::format f, char* buf, size_t len) const
functions.description: Retrieves clipboard data in the specified format into the provided buffer. Use get_data_length() first to size your buffer appropriately.
requirements: A successful lock must be held (locked() must be true).
f must be a valid format identifier.
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len should not exceed the available data length for the format (query via get_data_length()).

functions.name: clip::lock::get_data_length
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the clipboard data for the specified format. Typically used to size a buffer before calling get_data().
requirements: A successful lock should be held (locked() == true).
f must be a valid format identifier.

functions.name: clip::lock::set_image
functions.description: Sets an image to the clipboard using the provided image object. The library handles platform-specific conversions (e.g., premultiplied alpha on Windows).
requirements: A successful lock must be held (locked() must be true).
The input image should be valid (image.is_valid() == true).
Image data must represent straight (non‑premultiplied) RGB(A) as per library notes.

functions.name: clip::lock::get_image
functions.description: Retrieves the current clipboard image into the provided image object. Returned image data uses straight (non‑premultiplied) alpha.
requirements: A successful lock must be held (locked() must be true).
image will be modified on success; it should be in a state where reassignment is allowed.

functions.name: clip::lock::get_image_spec
functions.description: Retrieves only the image specification (dimensions, pixel layout, masks) of the clipboard image without transferring pixel data.
requirements: A successful lock must be held (locked() must be true).
spec is an output parameter and will be overwritten on success.

functions.name: clip::register_format
functions.description: Registers or retrieves a clipboard format identifier by name for use with set_data/get_data. Returned identifier is used to refer to that format.
requirements: name should identify the desired custom format. No explicit constraints documented.
Use the returned format with clip::lock::set_data/get_data or clip::has.

functions.name: clip::empty_format
functions.description: Returns the format identifier representing an empty clipboard (no content). Useful for comparisons or checks.
requirements: None beyond normal usage.

functions.name: clip::text_format
functions.description: Returns the format identifier used when the clipboard contains UTF‑8 text.
requirements: Use with has(), lock::is_convertible(), lock::set_data/get_data as appropriate.

functions.name: clip::image_format
functions.description: Returns the format identifier used when the clipboard contains an image.
requirements: Use with has(), lock operations, or format checks.

functions.name: clip::has
functions.description: High‑level query that returns true if the clipboard currently has content convertible to the given format.
requirements: f must be a valid format identifier.

functions.name: clip::clear
functions.description: High‑level function that clears the clipboard content without manually managing a lock.
requirements: None documented; returns false on error.

functions.name: clip::set_error_handler
functions.description: Sets a global error handler callback that receives ErrorCode values for clipboard-related errors (e.g., CannotLock, ImageNotSupported).
requirements: f must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(ErrorCode).
The handler should be reentrant/safe to call from library error contexts.

functions.name: clip::get_error_handler
functions.description: Returns the currently installed global error handler callback, or nullptr if none has been set.
requirements: None.

functions.name: clip::set_text
functions.description: High‑level API to set UTF‑8 text into the clipboard. Returns false on error.
requirements: value must contain UTF‑8 encoded text.

functions.name: clip::get_text
functions.description: High‑level API to get UTF‑8 text from the clipboard. On success, writes the text to value. Returns false on error or if not available.
requirements: value is an output parameter and will be overwritten on success.

functions.name: clip::image_spec::required_data_size
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to store an image with this specification. Likely derived from height * bytes_per_row. Exact formula is not shown in this header.
requirements: spec fields (width, height, bytes_per_row, bits_per_pixel, masks/shifts) should be set consistently; otherwise the result may be meaningless.

functions.name: clip::image::image
functions.description: Default constructs an empty/invalid image object (no owned data).
requirements: None.

functions.name: clip::image::image
functions.description: Constructs an image with the given specification and allocates/owns pixel storage accordingly.
requirements: spec fields must describe a valid pixel layout. The amount of data implied by spec must be allocatable.
Image data is expected to be straight (non‑premultiplied) alpha per library notes.

functions.name: clip::image::image
functions.signature: clip::image::image(const void* data, const clip::image_spec& spec)
functions.description: Constructs an image that references/copies pixel data described by spec from the provided memory. The image will represent straight (non‑premultiplied) alpha data.
requirements: data must point to at least the number of bytes required by spec (e.g., spec.required_data_size()).
spec must be valid and consistent with the data pointer.
Input data should be straight (non‑premultiplied) alpha.

functions.name: clip::image::image
functions.description: Copy constructor. Creates a deep copy of the given image, including its specification and pixel data.
requirements: The source image may be valid or invalid; behavior follows standard copy semantics.

functions.name: clip::image::image
functions.description: Move constructor. Transfers ownership of image data/spec from the source image to this one, leaving the source in a moved‑from state.
requirements: Source image becomes moved‑from; do not rely on its previous contents.

functions.name: clip::image::~image
functions.description: Destructor that frees any owned pixel data and cleans up resources.
requirements: Do not use the image after destruction.

functions.name: clip::image::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Replaces this image with a deep copy of another image’s spec and data.
requirements: Both images may be the same object; should handle self‑assignment safely (typical expectation).

functions.name: clip::image::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Transfers ownership of pixel data/spec from the source image to this one.
requirements: After the move, the source becomes moved‑from and should not be used except for destruction or reassignment.

functions.name: clip::image::data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the underlying pixel data buffer. The method is const but returns a modifiable pointer; modifying the data through this pointer alters the image contents.
requirements: The image must be valid (is_valid() == true) for the pointer to be non‑null.
Do not read/write beyond the allocated size (e.g., spec.required_data_size()).

functions.name: clip::image::spec
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the image specification (dimensions, pixel format, masks/shifts, bytes per row).
requirements: The returned reference remains valid while the image object remains alive and unmodified in ways that replace its spec.

functions.name: clip::image::is_valid
functions.description: Returns true if the image currently has an associated data buffer (non‑null).
requirements: None.

functions.name: clip::image::reset
functions.description: Resets the image to an invalid/empty state, releasing owned data and clearing the specification appropriately.
requirements: After reset, previously obtained data pointers become invalid.

functions.name: clip::set_image
functions.description: High‑level API to place an image on the clipboard. Handles platform‑specific conversions automatically. Returns false on error.
requirements: img should be valid (img.is_valid() == true).
Image data must be straight (non‑premultiplied) alpha as per library notes.

functions.name: clip::get_image
functions.description: High‑level API to retrieve an image from the clipboard into img. The returned image data uses straight alpha. Returns false on error.
requirements: img will be modified on success.

functions.name: clip::get_image_spec
functions.description: High‑level API to query the clipboard image specification without transferring pixel data. Returns false on error.
requirements: spec is an output parameter and will be overwritten on success.

functions.name: clip::set_x11_wait_timeout
functions.description: X11-only: Sets the timeout in milliseconds to wait for the selection/clipboard owner to receive content. Default is 1000 ms.
requirements: Only meaningful on X11 platforms; has no effect on others.
msecs should be a non‑negative integer.

functions.name: clip::get_x11_wait_timeout
functions.description: X11-only: Returns the current timeout in milliseconds used when waiting for the selection/clipboard owner.
requirements: Only meaningful on X11 platforms.

data_types.description: An unconstrained byte buffer with any values 0x00–0xFF. May include NUL bytes and is not required to be valid text or encoded data. Used when APIs expect raw bytes with an explicit length.

A generic string of bytes interpreted as a name/identifier. No specific encoding or character constraints implied beyond being a sequence of bytes; typical use is ASCII/UTF-8, but arbitrary bytes may appear.
A string containing valid UTF-8 encoded textual data, potentially including common whitespace such as newline, carriage return, and tab. For clipboard text-oriented APIs expecting UTF-8.

import os
import random
from typing import List

# Generator for arbitrary binary data payloads to be used with clip::lock::set_data
# Constraints from the stub:
# - Non-empty buffer
# - Length bounded: the stub truncates to 1024 bytes; keep <= 1024
# - Any bytes 0x00..0xFF are valid
# - Aim to produce varied yet valid payloads that may trigger different code paths
#   in consumers (e.g., containing NULs, printable text, repeating patterns, high-entropy, etc.)

MAX_SIZE = 1024

def _rand(rng: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(a, b)

def _pattern_repeating(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a repeating pattern from a randomly chosen motif
    motifs: List[bytes] = []
    # Common small motifs
    motifs.append(b"\x00")
    motifs.append(b"\xff")
    motifs.append(b"\x00\xff")
    motifs.append(b"\x55\xaa")
    motifs.append(b"\xde\xad\xbe\xef")
    # Random motif
    mlen = _rand(rng, 1, 16)
    motifs.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(mlen)))
    motif = rng.choice(motifs)
    total = _rand(rng, 1, MAX_SIZE)
    rep = (motif * (total // len(motif) + 1))[:total]
    return rep

def _pattern_structured_text(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # UTF-8 printable text with various line endings and lengths
    words = [
        "Hello, world!", "clipboard", "text", "image", "format", "UTF-8",
        "null\x00byte", "CRLF\r\n", "LF\n", "tabs\tindent", "unicode – αβγ", "end"
    ]
    # Compose several lines
    lines = []
    for _ in range(_rand(rng, 2, 10)):
        w = rng.choice(words)
        # Occasionally append numbers or hex-like tokens
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            w += f" {rng.randint(0, 1<<16):04x}"
        # Occasionally include NULs inside
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            w = w + "\x00" + rng.choice(words)
        lines.append(w)
    sep = rng.choice(["\n", "\r\n", "\r", "\n\n"]) 
    s = sep.join(lines)
    b = s.encode("utf-8", errors="surrogatepass")
    if len(b) > MAX_SIZE:
        b = b[:MAX_SIZE]
    if not b:
        b = b"A"
    return b

def _pattern_high_entropy(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    size = _rand(rng, 16, MAX_SIZE)
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))

def _pattern_ring_and_edges(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix of 0x00, 0xFF, ascending/descending sequences to probe edge handling
    size = _rand(rng, 32, MAX_SIZE)
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Header with size and magic
    magic = b"CLIP" + size.to_bytes(2, 'little', signed=False)
    parts.append(magic)
    # Ascending sequence
    asc_len = _rand(rng, 8, 64)
    parts.append(bytes((i % 256 for i in range(asc_len))))
    # Descending sequence
    desc_len = _rand(rng, 8, 64)
    parts.append(bytes(((255 - i) % 256 for i in range(desc_len))))
    # Zero run
    parts.append(b"\x00" * _rand(rng, 0, 64))
    # FF run
    parts.append(b"\xff" * _rand(rng, 0, 64))
    # Random tail
    tail_len = max(0, size - sum(len(p) for p in parts))
    parts.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(tail_len)))
    data = b"".join(parts)[:MAX_SIZE]
    if not data:
        data = b"X"
    return data

def _pattern_partial_utf8_with_nuls(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix valid UTF-8, embedded NULs, and truncated multibyte sequences
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    # Valid UTF-8 chunk
    valid = "😊 clipboard 📋 data 🔣".encode("utf-8")
    chunks.append(valid[:_rand(rng, 4, len(valid))])
    # NULs interleaved
    chunks.append(b"\x00" * _rand(rng, 1, 16))
    # Another text chunk
    more = "résumé – café – naïve".encode("utf-8")
    chunks.append(more[:_rand(rng, 4, len(more))])
    # Optional truncated multibyte prefix to test consumers that read len strictly
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        # Start of a 3-byte sequence 0xE2 0x82 0xAC (Euro) but possibly cut
        euro = b"\xE2\x82\xAC"
        cut = _rand(rng, 1, 2)
        chunks.append(euro[:cut])
    # Random filler
    filler = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(_rand(rng, 0, 32)))
    chunks.append(filler)
    data = b"".join(chunks)
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]
    if not data:
        data = b"Y"
    return data

def _pattern_length_prefixed(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Simple length-prefixed payload (not required by API but often exercised)
    body_len = _rand(rng, 1, MAX_SIZE - 8)
    body_type = rng.choice([
        b"TXT", b"BIN", b"IMG", b"DAT", b"RAW"
    ])
    body = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(body_len))
    header = b"LEN\x00" + len(body).to_bytes(4, 'little', signed=False) + body_type
    out = header + body
    return out[:MAX_SIZE]

def _ensure_non_empty(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return data if data else b"Z"

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a pattern family to diversify payloads while keeping them valid
    builders = [
        _pattern_repeating,
        _pattern_structured_text,
        _pattern_high_entropy,
        _pattern_ring_and_edges,
        _pattern_partial_utf8_with_nuls,
        _pattern_length_prefixed,
    ]
    # Optionally concatenate two small patterns to increase variety while respecting size
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        a = rng.choice(builders)(rng)
        b = rng.choice(builders)(rng)
        combined = (a + b)[:MAX_SIZE]
        return _ensure_non_empty(combined)
    else:
        data = rng.choice(builders)(rng)
        return _ensure_non_empty(data)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: arbitrary string used as a clipboard custom format name
# The fuzzer stub caps the name length to 128 bytes. We generate interesting
# byte sequences up to 128 bytes. Avoid embedding literal NULs in source; any
# NULs are produced via bytes construction, not string literals.

MAX_LEN = 128

_ascii_printable = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:+[](){}#@!$%^&=,~"

# Some interesting Unicode sequences (UTF-8) including combining marks, emoji, RTL, CJK
_unicode_samples: List[str] = [
    "",  # empty
    "A",  # simple
    "ClipboardFormat",
    "text/plain",
    "application/x-custom",
    "格式",  # CJK
    "формат",  # Cyrillic
    "اسم",  # Arabic
    "नाम",  # Devanagari
    "🙂",  # emoji
    "👍🏽",  # emoji + skin tone
    "e\x1b\u0000",  # ESC + NUL via escapes
    "a\u0000a",
    "Z\u0000d",
    "\u0000f\u0000f\u0000f",
    "\u0000",  # single NUL
    "\u0006a\u0006f\u0006e",
    "\u000b\u000c\r",  # VT, FF, CR
    "\n\n\n",  # newlines
    "\r\n",  # CRLF
]

_common_like = [
    "CF_TEXT", "CF_UNICODETEXT", "CF_BITMAP", "CF_DIB", "CF_DIBV5",
    "text/uri-list", "text/html", "text/plain;charset=utf-8",
    "image/png", "image/bmp", "image/jpeg", "application/json",
]

def rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))


def mix_segments(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.30:
            l = rng.randint(1, 32)
            parts.append(''.join(rng.choice(_ascii_printable) for _ in range(l)).encode('utf-8'))
        elif choice < 0.55:
            s = rng.choice(_unicode_samples)
            if not s:
                s = ''.join(rng.choice(['格式', '🙂', '名', '漢', '字', '😀', 'α', 'β', 'γ']) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)))
            parts.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass'))
        elif choice < 0.80:
            parts.append(rng.choice(_common_like).encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            parts.append(rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 24)))
    data = b''.join(parts)
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and len(data) > 0:
        idx = rng.randrange(0, len(data)+1)
        data = data[:idx] + (b"\x00" * rng.randint(1, 3)) + data[idx:]
    return data


def edge_case(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    cases = []
    cases.append(b"")  # empty
    cases.append(b"A")
    cases.append(b"a" * MAX_LEN)  # max length ASCII
    cases.append(b"\x00" * MAX_LEN)  # max length NULs
    # "image/png\0" + padding to MAX_LEN constructed without literal NUL in source
    prefix = b"image/png" + b"\x00"
    if len(prefix) < MAX_LEN:
        cases.append(prefix + b"X" * (MAX_LEN - len(prefix)))
    else:
        cases.append(prefix[:MAX_LEN])
    cases.append(b"text/plain;charset=utf-8")
    cases.append(b"CF_UNICODETEXT")
    uni = ("😀" * 100).encode('utf-8')
    cases.append(uni[:MAX_LEN])
    cases.append(bytes([i % 256 for i in range(MAX_LEN)]))
    return rng.choice(cases)


def clamp(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(b) <= MAX_LEN:
        return b
    return b[:MAX_LEN]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    p = rng.random()
    if p < 0.30:
        data = edge_case(rng)
    elif p < 0.85:
        data = mix_segments(rng)
    else:
        mode = rng.randrange(4)
        if mode == 0:
            n = rng.randint(0, MAX_LEN)
            data = ''.join(rng.choice(_ascii_printable) for _ in range(n)).encode('utf-8')
        elif mode == 1:
            s = ''.join(rng.choice([
                '🙂', '👍🏽', '格式', '名', '漢', '字', 'α', 'β', 'γ', 'Ж', 'Ω', '𝛑'
            ]) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 64)))
            data = s.encode('utf-8')
        elif mode == 2:
            data = rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, MAX_LEN))
        else:
            mime = rng.choice(['text/plain', 'text/html', 'application/json', 'application/x-foo', 'image/png', 'image/bmp'])
            params = []
            if rng.random() < 0.7:
                params.append('charset=' + rng.choice(['utf-8', 'utf-16', 'iso-8859-1']))
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                params.append('version=' + str(rng.randint(1, 5)))
            if params:
                mime = mime + ';' + ';'.join(params)
            if rng.random() < 0.4:
                mime += ";name=" + ''.join(rng.choice(_ascii_printable) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 16)))
            data = mime.encode('utf-8')

    return clamp(data)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Provide valid UTF-8 text bytes that the fuzzer stub will further
# sanitize to ASCII subset. We should generate interesting, valid UTF-8 that,
# after the stub's filtering (allowing \n, \r, \t, and 0x20..0x7E), still leaves
# meaningful content. We keep size <= 1024 because the stub truncates above that.

ASCII_PRINTABLE = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x20, 0x7F))
ALLOWED_CHARS = ASCII_PRINTABLE + "\n\r\t"

# Useful building blocks to explore different clipboard text behaviors
COMMON_LINES = [
    "",  # empty will be replaced in stub, but we can mix empty lines
    "A",
    "Hello, world!",
    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
    "1234567890",
    "!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:'\",.<>/?`~",
    "\tIndented line",
    "Line with spaces    ",
    "Multiple\nlines\nwith\nLF",
    "CRLF\r\nline endings",
    "Tabs\tand\ttabs",
    "Unicode names (will be ASCII here): cafe, resume, naive",
]

# Generate various newline styles
NEWLINE_STYLES = ["\n", "\r\n", "\r"]

# Random ASCII word generator
def rand_word(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    letters = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(letters) for _ in range(n))

# Random line with punctuation and whitespace
def rand_line(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    chars = ALLOWED_CHARS
    return ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(target_len))

def make_blocks(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    blocks: List[str] = []

    # Include a selection of canned lines
    canned = rng.sample(COMMON_LINES, k=rng.randint(3, min(8, len(COMMON_LINES))))
    blocks.extend(canned)

    # Add random words/sentences
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        words = [rand_word(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 15))]
        sep = rng.choice([" ", "\t"])  # include tabs occasionally
        sentence = sep.join(words)
        # Optionally add punctuation
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            sentence += rng.choice([".", "?", "!", ":", ";"])
        blocks.append(sentence)

    # Add lines with specific control chars
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        blocks.append("".join(["A", "\n", "B", "\t", "C", "\r", "D"]))

    # Add long random ASCII line
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        blocks.append(rand_line(rng, rng.randint(40, 200)))

    return blocks

def assemble_text(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    blocks = make_blocks(rng)

    # Randomly choose a newline style for joining
    join_nl = rng.choice(NEWLINE_STYLES)

    # Shuffle to vary structure
    rng.shuffle(blocks)

    text = join_nl.join(blocks)

    # Optionally add a trailing newline style
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        text += join_nl

    # Ensure non-empty and within size cap before stub truncation (<= 1024)
    # We bias lengths to a variety of sizes.
    max_len = 1024
    if not text:
        text = "A"

    # Occasionally craft edge-case lengths around boundaries
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        target = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1023, 1024])
        if len(text) < target:
            # pad with allowed chars
            pad_char = rng.choice(list(ALLOWED_CHARS))
            text = text + pad_char * (target - len(text))
        else:
            text = text[:target]

    # Otherwise, clamp to limit
    if len(text) > max_len:
        text = text[:max_len]

    # Guarantee that text contains at least one allowed character the stub keeps
    # (which it will, given our generation), and avoid being all whitespace sometimes
    if text.strip(" \t\r\n") == "" and len(text) < max_len:
        text += "A"

    return text

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a scenario to diversify content while remaining valid UTF-8 ASCII
    scenario = rng.choice([
        "sentences",
        "csv",
        "tsv",
        "json_like",
        "path_list",
        "code_like",
        "poem",
    ])

    if scenario == "sentences":
        text = assemble_text(rng)
    elif scenario == "csv":
        rows = rng.randint(3, 40)
        cols = rng.randint(2, 8)
        lines = []
        for _ in range(rows):
            row = []
            for _c in range(cols):
                cell = rand_word(rng, 0, 10)
                # Occasionally quote and include commas/space
                if rng.random() < 0.4:
                    cell = '"' + cell + ("," if rng.random() < 0.5 else "") + '"'
                row.append(cell)
            lines.append(','.join(row))
        text = "\n".join(lines)
    elif scenario == "tsv":
        rows = rng.randint(3, 40)
        cols = rng.randint(2, 12)
        lines = []
        for _ in range(rows):
            row = [rand_word(rng, 0, 16) for _ in range(cols)]
            lines.append("\t".join(row))
        text = "\n".join(lines)
    elif scenario == "json_like":
        # ASCII-only pseudo-JSON, valid UTF-8
        pairs = []
        n = rng.randint(3, 20)
        for i in range(n):
            k = f"key{i}_{rand_word(rng,1,6)}"
            v_choice = rng.random()
            if v_choice < 0.4:
                v = f'"{rand_word(rng,0,10)}"'
            elif v_choice < 0.7:
                v = str(rng.randint(-100000, 100000))
            else:
                v = "true" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "false"
            pairs.append(f'"{k}": {v}')
        text = "{" + ", ".join(pairs) + "}"
    elif scenario == "path_list":
        # Simulate file paths (ASCII), separated by various newlines
        roots = ["/", "C:/", "D:/", "./", "../"]
        parts = ["usr", "bin", "lib", "home", "tmp", "var", "etc", "Documents", "Downloads"]
        lines = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 40)):
            root = rng.choice(roots)
            depth = rng.randint(1, 6)
            segs = [rng.choice(parts) for _ in range(depth)]
            # Mix separators
            sep = rng.choice(["/", "\\\\"])  # escaped backslash for Python string
            path = root + sep.join(segs)
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                path += rng.choice([".txt", ".bin", ".png", ".json"]) 
            lines.append(path)
        text = rng.choice(NEWLINE_STYLES).join(lines)
    elif scenario == "code_like":
        # Simple ASCII pseudo-code snippet
        keywords = ["if", "else", "for", "while", "return", "int", "char", "void", "bool", "true", "false"]
        ops = ["+", "-", "*", "/", "%", "==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "&&", "||"]
        lines = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 60)):
            line = []
            if rng.random() < 0.4:
                line.append(rng.choice(keywords))
            line.append(rand_word(rng,1,10))
            if rng.random() < 0.7:
                line.append(rng.choice(ops))
                line.append(rand_word(rng,1,10))
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                line.append(";")
            lines.append(" ".join(line))
        text = "\n".join(lines)
    elif scenario == "poem":
        # Lines with varied lengths and whitespace
        lines = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 40)):
            length = rng.randint(0, 80)
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                lines.append("")
            else:
                lines.append(rand_line(rng, length).rstrip())
        text = "\n".join(lines)
    else:
        text = assemble_text(rng)

    # Final size clamp to 4096 overall requirement and stub's 1024; keep <= 1024
    text = text[:1024]

    # Ensure valid UTF-8 ASCII bytes
    data = text.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    return data
